stack_version_constraints.tauri: No native Rust change in this slice.

issue_discussion_notes: No new library or public API risk was introduced. Official React/MDN docs and local source contracts were sufficient for this narrow renderer lifecycle change.
community_signal_notes: No community popularity signal was used as factual proof.
language_decision_notes: The bottleneck is component mount and tab render lifecycle, so the renderer is the direct control point. Rust cache remains useful for file IO but cannot keep React tab state mounted.
architecture_options: Resident mounted section panels with idle preloading
Immediate all-tab mount on first render
architecture_decision_notes: Resident mounted panels with idle preloading best matches the user's memory-first desktop request while avoiding a single startup CPU spike.
architecture_practitioner_sources: Existing local MountedSectionPanel pattern for source workbench
architecture_tradeoff_notes: The design trades higher steady-state memory for lower tab transition mount cost. Hidden panels remain mounted but are accessibility-hidden and layout-contained.
code_reference_notes: The source workbench already used MountedSectionPanel to preserve editor state. This slice generalizes that pattern across all primary tabs.
folder_structure_options: Create a new resident section manager component
folder_structure_decision_notes: The existing shell owns section activation, visible sections, and toolbar state, so a narrow patch avoids a speculative abstraction.
folder_semantics_notes: No new source folder was created. Spec/history records use the existing project-specific requirements/spec locations.
maintainability_notes: If resident section policy gains user settings or memory budgets, extract the scheduler into a small hook.
